description: How a reader reaches and trusts a feed. It names environment variables, never secrets, so it can be emailed or committed.

age_identity.description: Never a value. A connection file holds no secret; age_identity_env names the variable that holds the age identity.
age_identity.x-note: A literal age identity here would put a secret in a file meant to be emailed or committed.

age_identity_env.description: The variable holding the age identity. Required for an encrypted feed.

auth.description: How the reader authenticates. Every secret is named by an environment variable, in a field ending _env.

access_key_id.description: Never a value. A connection file holds no secret; access_key_id_env names the variable that holds the access key id.
access_key_id.x-note: A literal access key id here would put a secret in a file meant to be emailed or committed.

access_key_id_env.description: For s3, the variable holding the access key id.

client_secret.description: Never a value. A connection file holds no secret; client_secret_env names the variable that holds the client secret.
client_secret.x-note: A literal client secret here would put a secret in a file meant to be emailed or committed.

client_secret_env.description: For oauth-client-credentials, the variable holding the client secret.

method.description: What the reader sends; the fields a method needs are required for it.

secret_access_key.description: Never a value. A connection file holds no secret; secret_access_key_env names the variable that holds the secret access key.
secret_access_key.x-note: A literal secret access key here would put a secret in a file meant to be emailed or committed.

secret_access_key_env.description: For s3, the variable holding the secret access key.

token.description: Never a value. A connection file holds no secret; token_env names the variable that holds the token.
token.x-note: A literal token here would put a secret in a file meant to be emailed or committed.

token_env.description: For bearer, the variable holding the token.

feed.description: The feed's id, <publisher>/<slug>. Its feed.json must have this id.

keys.description: Pinned keys. Absent or empty means use the publisher's key set, and ask before trusting it the first time.

id.description: The key's id within its publisher.

public_key.description: The 32-byte public key, base64url without padding.

location.description: Where the feed's files are. The fields a kind needs are required for it, which the reader enforces.

kind.description: https needs url; s3 needs endpoint, region, bucket and prefix.

path_style.description: For s3, address the bucket in the path rather than the host name. False when absent.

prefix.description: For s3, the key prefix the feed's files are under, empty or ending in a slash.

url.description: For https, the feed's base URL, ending in a slash.

title: feed-connection
